packages/herdr/scripts/tests/test_run_in_pane.sh starts the --exec wrapper with HERDR_PANE_ID set, which runs 'sleep infinity' to keep the pane alive. The test kills the wrapper bash PID but not the grandchild 'sleep infinity', which is reparented to init and inherits the script's stdout. Any invocation piped to tail/head (e.g. 'bash test_run_in_pane.sh 2>&1 | tail -35') therefore never sees EOF and hangs indefinitely, even under 'timeout N' (timeout kills the direct child; the orphan keeps the pipe open). This caused multiple driven child sessions to hang during WL-0MUKZGEQ2007FECS. Suggested fix: kill the whole process group / reap the grandchild (e.g. run the background wrapper via setsid and kill the group, or track and kill the 'sleep infinity' PID), and/or send its output to a file rather than a pipe.
data.title: run-in-pane test leaks orphaned sleep infinity that hangs piped invocations

phase_finish fast-forwards the main checkout's local dev to origin/dev (git fetch + 'git merge --ff-only origin/dev') and then attempts 'git merge --ff-only <child commit>' — but the child branch was forked from the older dev tip, so the merge fails non-fast-forward. The failure is only a warning, so the subsequent 'git push origin <branch>:refs/heads/dev' is rejected (non-fast-forward) and finish resets the item to open. Any concurrent push to dev by another agent triggers this. Worked around manually during WL-0MUKZGEQ2007FECS: recreate the worktree, 'git rebase origin/dev', push. Suggested fix: before pushing, rebase/merge the feature branch onto origin/dev (or retry by rebasing when the push is rejected).
data.title: implement.py finish fails non-fast-forward when dev advances during the run
